territorial_scope.description: Covers AI companion users within the State of New Jersey; the text does not state a location requirement for operators.

evidence.quote: any individual who uses an AI companion for personal use within the State

summary.short: Would require operators of AI companion systems to notify users that they are not communicating with a human, at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours thereafter. Violations would carry a $15,000 civil penalty per violation. Would take effect immediately on enactment.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill would apply to operators of 'artificial intelligence companion' systems: systems using generative AI designed to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by retaining information from prior interactions, asking unprompted emotion-based questions, and sustaining personal dialogue. Operators, defined to include members, affiliates, subsidiaries and beneficial owners of firms that operate or provide such a system, would have to give clear and conspicuous notice to a user, verbally or in writing, at the beginning of any AI companion interaction that the user is not communicating with a human. The notice would repeat at least every three hours during continued interaction. 'User' means an individual using an AI companion for personal use within New Jersey who is not an operator, agent or affiliate. Operators that violate the act would be subject to a civil penalty of $15,000 per violation, collected in a civil action by summary proceeding under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999; the Superior Court and municipal court would have jurisdiction. The act would take effect immediately.

relations.note: Sec. 3 provides that the civil penalty is to be collected in a civil action by summary proceeding under this law, and that the Superior Court and municipal court have jurisdiction to enforce that law's provisions under the section.

evidence.quote: to be collected in a civil action by a summary proceeding under the "Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999," P.L.1999, c.274 (C.2A:58-10 et seq.)

notes: Introduced bill text; the citation 'P.L. ,c. (C. )' is a placeholder that refers to this bill itself and is not coded as a relation. The Statement says notice is provided 'periodically throughout' the interaction; Sec. 2 specifies repetition at least every three hours. Sec. 1 uses 'human or human-like relationship' and 'to facilitate' while the Statement uses 'relationships' and 'facilitate' without 'to'; the substance is the same. No amendments, repeals or legal basis are stated.

events.date_text: This act shall take effect immediately.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff that changes who is in scope, eligible, exempt or subject to a higher obligation tier. The $15,000 figure in Sec. 3 is a civil penalty per violation and is recorded under enforcement, not thresholds. The three-hour repeat interval in Sec. 2 is a parameter of the notification obligation, not a legal cutoff. No age, size or user-count limits appear.
